object.text:
# FrostOps-Lab

Well, this repository used to replicate little steps towards DevOps—sadly, no preference remains unhalted forever.

I noticed that I started liking the idea of working with something more advanced... like AI!—while keeping some DevOps quirks.

I had a LOT of plans for this repository. I thought about deleting the whole "sentinel-cli" and calling it "cruddy", it had much more value in my eyes. What "cruddy" was meant to be:
*   Based on reading logs or any messy output and making a human-readable output on the terminal (using the Charmbracelet ecosystem).
*   Meant to have `cruddy db <databaseName>` - this would have run that database automatically.
*   The human-readable output wasn't just a simplified version, but included:
    *   **The Error**
    *   **The Cause**
    *   **The Recommendation**
    *   **The Fix** (if it had a command to fix it)

But whatever, it's not like the skills I learned over time will disappear into thin air!

o7

object.text:
# Prolepsis

> A high-performance developer data ETL pipeline and context engine designed to aggregate multi-platform user telemetry into PostgreSQL, providing rich, structured context for AI interactions.

> To check how the architrecture works, [clicke me](https://github.com/shawnfrost25/prolepsis/tree/main/docs/visualization)

---

## Disclaimer

**Note:** This project is under active development. Core features are being implemented and tested rapidly, so APIs and functionality may break between commits as the architecture evolves. Most of the test and functions are temporary—only when the README.md is fully updated everything will be considered "finale-finale."

---

## Core Purpose

**Prolepsis** is an active ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) backend engineered to continuously fetch, normalize, and store a user's digital footprint across multiple platforms. By centralizing this data inside a structured PostgreSQL database, the system serves as a rich context provider, giving AI models deep, accurate visibility into the user's background, repositories, coding activity, and professional history during conversations.

---

## Key Features & Modules

* **Multi-Platform ETL Ingestion:**
  - **GitHub Integration:** Robust OAuth2 authentication and webhook event handling tracking pushes, commits, pull requests, issues, issue comments, and releases.
  - **Platform Connectors:** Extensible pipeline modules for aggregating developer metrics across platforms like **LeetCode**, **StackOverflow**, **etc...**
* **Rust gRPC PDF Extraction Sidecar:**
  - High-performance document parsing service built in Rust (using `tonic` and `prost`) to extract structured text and metadata from PDF files (with OCR capabilities planned).
* **Kitanai API & User Management:**
  - Complete backend lifecycle management: user registration, login, profile queries, session validation, and account verification.
  - Secure automated background job queues (via `River`) handling scheduled data deletions and cleanup tasks.
* **Session & Token Management:**
  - High-speed session management and token validation powered by Redis.

---

## Tech Stack & Architecture

* **Backend Core:** Go (Golang) microservice architecture.
* **gRPC Sidecar:** Rust (`tonic`, `prost`) for heavy document/PDF processing.
* **Database & Migrations:** PostgreSQL managed with **Atlas** schema migrations and type-safe query generation via **sqlc** (`pgxpool`).
* **Caching & Jobs:** Redis for session caching and state management; River for background job processing.
* **Containerization:** Docker & Docker Compose for multi-container orchestration (`compose.yaml`).

---

## Future Ideas
* **Rust Sidecar OCR Fallback:** Integrating an OCR fallback mechanism into the Rust PDF extraction sidecar to seamlessly process documents whenever `pdf_oxide` fails.
* **Advanced Telemetry:** Implementing robust observability and monitoring pipelines utilizing OpenTelemetry, Grafana Alloy, Grafana dashboards, and planned Prometheus integration.
* **Cloud & Infrastructure as Code:** Provisioning and managing cloud architecture on AWS using Terraform and OpenTofu with HCL syntax, remote state locking, and strict cost guardrails.
* **Kubernetes Orchestration:** Deploying services on Kubernetes via k3d using Helm charts, health probes, resource limits, and automated rolling updates with fast rollback capabilities.
* **Production-Grade Testing:** Elevating the test suite to mimic real-world production environments using containerized dependencies (Testcontainers), chaos-replay verification streams, and rigorous race detection.
* **GitHub App Migration:** Migrating the webhook creation to GitHub App.

---
## Note on Development and AI usage
* **AI Usage:** AI was used exclusively for low-value, repetitive tasks—primarily boilerplate and test scaffolding (such as sqlc test.sql queries and Redis test fixtures like create_session.redis). These represent pure busywork not worth writing by hand. AI also assisted with occasional debugging sessions when root causes weren’t immediate, and with polishing code comments and documentation tone (this README being one example).
* **Author Implementation:** Every meaningful design decision, all core application logic, and virtually all actual source code were thought through and written by the author. The AI’s role was strictly limited to the minor, non-creative tasks listed above.

# Shawn Frost **Backend engineering, systems curiosity, and the occasional late-night debugging session.** Go · PostgreSQL · Redis · Rust · Distributed systems
“The feelings that hurt most, the emotions that sting most, are those that are absurd; the longing for impossible things, precisely because they are impossible; nostalgia for what never was; the desire for what could have been; regret over not being someone else; dissatisfaction with the world's existence. All these half-tones of the soul's consciousness create in us a painful landscape.”

— Fernando Pessoa, The Book of Disquiet
--- ## About I'm a backend-focused developer working primarily with **Go**, with a growing interest in systems programming, distributed services, and low-level runtime behavior. I like building software that stays reliable under failure, concurrency, load, and continuous change—not just software that works in a happy-path demo. I'm still learning constantly, but I'm comfortable going beyond beginner CRUD applications: I care about the trade-offs behind production-oriented design, useful tests, clear observability, and systems that remain understandable as they grow. I enjoy turning complex system behavior into clear mental models, and I like sharing what I learn through projects that are practical, measurable, and built to evolve. ## Comfort zone 1 (I Want To Love You Till Your Dying Day / KimiShinu)
## What I Know - **Go backend development:** HTTP APIs, `chi`, middleware, authentication, OAuth2, background workers, request lifecycles, concurrency, and error handling - **Data systems:** PostgreSQL, `pgx/pgxpool`, Squirrel, `sqlc`, Atlas migrations, relational modeling, constraints, indexes, transactions, and Redis - **Service architecture:** gRPC, Protocol Buffers, Go/Rust service boundaries, asynchronous jobs with River, retries, idempotency, and graceful shutdown - **Testing and reliability:** unit and integration tests, Testcontainers, race detection, HTTP handler and middleware testing, failure-oriented cases, and CI-based validation - **State and async tooling:** Redis-backed sessions with `go-redis`, scheduled/async job execution with River, and resilient retry/error workflows - **Security-minded backend work:** sessions, token handling, OAuth2 flows, webhook verification, input validation, and defensive error handling - **Infrastructure:** Docker Compose, GitHub Actions, Terraform/OpenTofu, Jenkins and GitLab CI/CD workflows, and Trivy image/filesystem scanning - **Observability:** structured logging with zerolog, Grafana Alloy, Loki, Grafana, contextual errors, cardinality awareness, and continued exploration of Prometheus and OpenTelemetry - **Engineering habits:** schema evolution, clean service boundaries, readable APIs, reproducible environments, and debugging systems under concurrency, failure, and load I don't measure engineering by the number of tools I can list. I care about understanding why a system behaves the way it does, choosing the simplest design that holds up under pressure, and writing tests that catch meaningful regressions instead of inflating a coverage percentage. ## Current Project **Prolepsis** is a developer-data ETL and context engine. It collects and normalizes activity from services such as GitHub, stores structured data in PostgreSQL, and exposes it as context for future AI interactions. The project brings together a Go API, GitHub OAuth and webhook ingestion, Redis sessions, River jobs, Atlas and sqlc, a RustPDF-processing gRPC sidecar, Docker Compose, integration tests, and separate Go/Rust CI pipelines. ## Comfort zone 2 (Cosmic Princess Kaguya / CPK)
> Comfort-zone GIFs were made by me (inspired by kattayan_46). > > The finale GIF is from kilianimes on GIPHY. ## What I'm Learning Next Better test design, deeper Go runtime and concurrency knowledge, more intentional telemetry, and practical distributed-systems design shaped by real failures rather than diagrams alone. ---
